name: Jie Long
description: Jie Long (接龙, connect dragon) is a Chinese domino connecting game. Players extend a single open end by playing a matching tile or discarding one face down. The player with fewest pips on discarded tiles wins; pairs settle by pip difference.

content.text: Jie Long (接龙, connect dragon) is a Chinese domino connecting game. Players extend a single open end by playing a matching tile or discarding one face down. The player with fewest pips on discarded tiles wins; pairs settle by pip difference.

Jie Long (接龙, connect dragon) is a Chinese domino connecting game; the name likens the chain of connected tiles to a dragon. Chinese dominoes date to the 12th or 13th century (earliest written mention in Hangzhou); the 32-tile set with civil and military tiles is traditional. Published rules and table traditions describe it as a single-arm game where a player unable to play must discard one tile face down, and the player with fewest pips on discarded tiles wins the deal. Related connecting games with the same discard-when-unable mechanic exist in Korea (Golpae) and Indonesia (Gaple).
32 Chinese dominoes (11 civil tiles x2, 10 military tiles x1; no blanks).
Chinese domino set or domino cards.

Four players: 8 tiles each. Three players: 10 tiles each, two tiles unused. Two players: 16 tiles each. First player for the first deal is chosen randomly; thereafter the winner of each deal plays first. Play is counter-clockwise.
